units.paraphrase: The RSO's duties also include overseeing implementation and resource allocation, addressing noncompliance reports, and making interpretive judgment calls.

units.excerpt: Internal transparency: We will share final, unredacted Risk Reports with Anthropic's regular-clearance staff.
units.paraphrase: Anthropic will share complete, unredacted Risk Reports with regular-clearance staff.

units.excerpt: Noncompliance reporting: We will maintain a process for Anthropic staff to submit anonymous or identified reports regarding potential noncompliance with this policy.
units.paraphrase: Anthropic will maintain a process for staff to report noncompliance, anonymously or identified.

units.excerpt: Staff will have more than one option for who receives these reports, including the RSO, and at least one executive who does not report to the RSO.
units.paraphrase: Staff can choose among multiple report recipients, including the RSO and an executive independent of the RSO.

units.excerpt: When we receive a report, we will promptly investigate, take appropriate and proportional corrective action if it is substantiated, and document the report and our findings.
units.paraphrase: Upon receiving a report, Anthropic will investigate promptly, take proportional corrective action if substantiated, and document findings.

units.excerpt: We will provide quarterly updates to the Board regarding reports of potential noncompliance, whether substantiated or not.
units.paraphrase: Anthropic will give the Board quarterly updates on noncompliance reports regardless of substantiation.

units.excerpt: If we determine that a report is (1) substantiated and (2) involves a material safety risk, we will promptly notify the Board and we may provide public notice of the same.
units.paraphrase: If a report is substantiated and involves material safety risk, the Board is promptly notified and public notice may follow.

units.excerpt: Finally, we will protect reporters from retaliation, and where a report concerns the conduct of the RSO, at least one recipient will be a member of the Board.
units.paraphrase: Anthropic will protect reporters from retaliation, and reports about the RSO must reach at least one Board member.

units.excerpt: Employee agreements: We will not impose contractual non-disparagement obligations on employees, candidates, or former employees in a way that could impede or discourage them from publicly raising safety concerns about Anthropic.
units.paraphrase: Anthropic will not use non-disparagement clauses that could discourage employees from raising safety concerns publicly.

units.excerpt: If we offer agreements with a non-disparagement clause, that clause will not preclude raising safety concerns, nor will it preclude disclosure of the existence of that clause.
units.paraphrase: Any non-disparagement clauses offered will not prevent raising safety concerns or disclosing the clause's existence.

units.excerpt: Internal review: We will regularly conduct an internal review of our implementation of this policy.
units.paraphrase: Anthropic will regularly review its own implementation of the policy.

units.excerpt: Procedural compliance review: On approximately an annual basis, we will commission a third-party review that assesses whether we adhered to this policy's main procedural commitments.
units.paraphrase: Anthropic will commission an annual third-party review of procedural adherence to the policy.

units.excerpt: This review will focus on procedural compliance, not substantive outcomes.
units.paraphrase: The compliance review addresses procedure only, not substantive results.

units.excerpt: Policy changes: Changes to the RSP will be proposed by the CEO and RSO, and approved by the Board in consultation with the LTBT.
units.paraphrase: RSP changes are proposed by the CEO and RSO and approved by the Board after consulting the LTBT.

units.excerpt: If we update the RSP, we will publicly share the updated version prior to or on its effective date and will record the differences from the prior draft in the Change Log.
units.paraphrase: Updated RSP versions are published by their effective date, with changes recorded in the Change Log.

units.excerpt: We will maintain the current version of the RSP on our website.
units.paraphrase: The current RSP version will be kept accessible on Anthropic's website.

units.section_heading: Appendix A: Commitments Related to Competitors
units.excerpt: These commitments are necessarily high-level and limited. In many cases, we will not have enough information to determine that the relevant scenario applies and will have to use our best judgment to deal with uncertainty.
units.paraphrase: The competitor-related commitments are general and their application will often require judgment calls due to uncertainty.

units.section_heading: Appendix A: Commitments Related to Competitors
units.excerpt: But to the extent that other relevant AI developers prioritize safety and invest in legible demonstrations that they are doing so—as we intend to—commitments like this may help avoid an inadvertent "race to the bottom" on safety.
units.paraphrase: If other developers similarly prioritize and demonstrate safety, these commitments may help prevent a safety race to the bottom.

units.section_heading: Appendix A: Commitments Related to Competitors
units.excerpt: Further, the commitments below do not preclude us from taking cautionary action, such as refraining from training or deploying models, in other circumstances.
units.paraphrase: These commitments do not limit Anthropic from taking other cautionary actions beyond what is specified.

units.section_heading: Appendix A: Commitments Related to Competitors
units.excerpt: Mitigating the risks from our models is a top priority for us, and we would strongly consider pausing development and/or deployment to improve the safety profiles of our models even in cases not covered below.
units.paraphrase: Risk mitigation is a top priority, and Anthropic would consider pausing development or deployment even in scenarios not otherwise addressed.

units.section_heading: Appendix A: Commitments Related to Competitors
units.locator: Table Appendix A / Anthropic in the lead / Scenario
units.context_stem: Row: Anthropic in the lead. Column: Scenario.
units.excerpt: We have developed or will imminently develop a highly capable model; and we have clear evidence that no other competitor will soon develop such a model.
units.paraphrase: The scenario is Anthropic having or imminently having a highly capable model with clear evidence no competitor is close behind.

units.section_heading: Appendix A: Commitments Related to Competitors
units.locator: Table Appendix A / Anthropic in the lead / Commitment
units.context_stem: Row: Anthropic in the lead. Column: Commitment.
units.excerpt: We will require a strong argument that catastrophic risk is contained, along the lines of our recommendations for industry-wide safety (see Section 1).
units.paraphrase: In this scenario, Anthropic requires a strong argument that catastrophic risk is contained, per its industry-wide safety recommendations.

units.section_heading: Appendix A: Commitments Related to Competitors
units.locator: Table Appendix A / Anthropic in the lead / Commitment
units.context_stem: Row: Anthropic in the lead. Column: Commitment.
units.excerpt: We will delay AI development and deployment as needed to achieve this, until and unless we no longer believe we have a significant lead.
units.paraphrase: Anthropic will delay development and deployment as necessary until it no longer believes it has a significant lead.

units.section_heading: Appendix A: Commitments Related to Competitors
units.locator: Table Appendix A / Competitors have strong safety measures / Scenario
units.context_stem: Row: Competitors have strong safety measures. Column: Scenario.
units.excerpt: We have strong evidence that all competitors who have developed, or will soon develop, a highly capable frontier model are able to make strong arguments that catastrophic risk is contained, in the spirit of our recommendations for industry-wide safety (see Section 1).
units.paraphrase: The scenario is strong evidence that all competitors with highly capable frontier models can argue catastrophic risk is contained.

units.section_heading: Appendix A: Commitments Related to Competitors
units.locator: Table Appendix A / Competitors have strong safety measures / Commitment
units.context_stem: Row: Competitors have strong safety measures. Column: Commitment.
units.excerpt: For our highly capable frontier models, we will meet or exceed the overall risk reduction posture of these competitors, as far as we can tell based on our best efforts to assess that posture.
units.paraphrase: Anthropic commits to meeting or exceeding competitors' risk reduction posture for its highly capable frontier models, based on best-effort assessment.

units.section_heading: Appendix A: Commitments Related to Competitors
units.locator: Table Appendix A / Competitors have strong safety measures / Commitment
units.context_stem: Row: Competitors have strong safety measures. Column: Commitment.
units.excerpt: Until we are able to do so, we will delay AI development and deployment as needed to achieve this.
units.paraphrase: Until it can meet or exceed that posture, Anthropic will delay development and deployment as needed.

units.section_heading: Appendix A: Commitments Related to Competitors
units.locator: Table Appendix A / General upleveling / Scenario
units.context_stem: Row: General upleveling. Column: Scenario, sub-item 1.
units.excerpt: We have strong evidence that a competitor has implemented a risk mitigation that: (1) represents a significant improvement on reduction of our prioritized risks relative to our analogous mitigations;
units.paraphrase: The scenario condition includes a competitor's mitigation being a significant improvement over Anthropic's analogous mitigation.

units.section_heading: Appendix A: Commitments Related to Competitors
units.locator: Table Appendix A / General upleveling / Scenario
units.context_stem: Row: General upleveling. Column: Scenario, sub-item 2.
units.excerpt: (2) we could implement at comparable (or lower) effort or cost to our competitor.
units.paraphrase: The second condition is that Anthropic could implement the mitigation at comparable or lower cost than the competitor.

units.section_heading: Appendix A: Commitments Related to Competitors
units.locator: Table Appendix A / General upleveling / Commitment
units.excerpt: We will make a significant effort to meet or exceed that performance standard. However, we will not necessarily delay AI development and deployment in this scenario.
units.paraphrase: Anthropic will make significant effort to match or exceed the standard but will not necessarily delay development or deployment.

units.excerpt: Earlier editions of our RSP defined "AI Safety Levels" with specific lists of required controls. We still use this concept to refer to, and distinguish between, present levels of risk mitigations—those that we maintain for existing AI models.
units.paraphrase: Prior RSP editions used ASLs with specific required controls; the concept still denotes present risk-mitigation levels for existing models.

units.excerpt: (For example, our initial Risk Report uses this distinction.)
units.paraphrase: An example is given: the initial Risk Report uses the present/future distinction.

units.excerpt: However, when defining the risk mitigations needed for future levels of AI capability, we have found that providing a specific list of controls is overly rigid, and we instead prefer to focus on what sort of argument an AI developer should make (and what sorts of actors it should address) regarding the risk level from its systems.
units.paraphrase: For future capability levels, Anthropic prefers argument-based reasoning over rigid control lists, focusing on the argument and relevant threat actors.

units.excerpt: RSP-2023 (aka RSP v1.0): Initial version.
units.paraphrase: The changelog entry for RSP v1.0 notes it as the initial version.

units.excerpt: RSP-2024: This update introduces a more flexible and nuanced approach to assessing and managing AI risks while maintaining our commitment not to train or deploy models unless we have implemented adequate safeguards.
units.paraphrase: The v2.0 update introduces a more flexible risk-management approach while retaining the commitment to adequate safeguards before training or deployment.

units.excerpt: Key improvements include new capability thresholds to indicate when we should upgrade our safeguards, refined processes for evaluating model capabilities and the adequacy of our safeguards (inspired by safety case methodologies), and new measures for internal governance and external input.
units.paraphrase: Key v2.0 improvements are new capability thresholds, refined evaluation processes inspired by safety cases, and new governance/external-input measures.

units.excerpt: We describe the most notable changes below.
units.paraphrase: The most notable changes are described in the following entries.

units.locator: Changelog / RSP v2.0 / ASL definition changed
units.excerpt: ASL definition changed: The term "ASL" now refers to groups of technical and operational safeguards (it previously also referred to models). We also introduced the new concepts of Capability Thresholds and Required Safeguards.
units.paraphrase: The ASL term was redefined to refer only to safeguard groups rather than models, alongside new Capability Threshold and Required Safeguard concepts.

units.locator: Changelog / RSP v2.0 / ASL definition changed
units.excerpt: This change allows for more targeted application of safeguards based on specific capabilities, rather than broad model categories.
units.paraphrase: The redefinition enables safeguards to be targeted at specific capabilities rather than broad model categories.

units.locator: Changelog / RSP v2.0 / ARA threshold now a checkpoint
units.excerpt: ARA threshold now a checkpoint: We replaced our previous autonomous replication and adaption (ARA) threshold with a "checkpoint" for autonomous AI capabilities.
units.paraphrase: The former ARA threshold was replaced with a checkpoint concept for autonomous AI capabilities.

units.locator: Changelog / RSP v2.0 / ARA threshold now a checkpoint
units.excerpt: Rather than triggering higher safety standards automatically, reaching this checkpoint will prompt additional evaluation of the model's capabilities and accelerate our preparation of stronger safeguards.
units.paraphrase: Reaching the checkpoint triggers further evaluation and accelerated safeguard preparation, rather than automatic standard upgrades.

units.locator: Changelog / RSP v2.0 / ARA threshold now a checkpoint
units.excerpt: We previously considered these capabilities as a trigger for increased safeguards, motivated by an attempt to establish some threshold while we developed a better sense of potential threats.
units.paraphrase: These capabilities were formerly treated as a safeguard trigger while understanding of threats was still developing.

units.locator: Changelog / RSP v2.0 / ARA threshold now a checkpoint
units.excerpt: We now believe that these capabilities - at the levels we initially considered - would not necessitate the ASL-3 standard.
units.paraphrase: Anthropic now believes the originally considered capability levels do not require the ASL-3 standard.

units.locator: Changelog / RSP v2.0 / AI R&D threshold added
units.excerpt: AI R&D threshold added: We added a new threshold for AI systems that can significantly advance AI development.
units.paraphrase: A new threshold was added for AI systems that can significantly advance AI development.

units.locator: Changelog / RSP v2.0 / AI R&D threshold added
units.excerpt: Such capabilities could lead to rapid, unpredictable advances in AI, potentially outpacing our ability to evaluate and address emerging risks, and may also serve as an early warning sign for the ability to automate R&D in other domains.
units.paraphrase: These capabilities risk causing rapid unpredictable advances outpacing risk evaluation, and may indicate broader R&D automation ability.

units.locator: Changelog / RSP v2.0 / Testing for Capability Thresholds
units.excerpt: Testing for Capability Thresholds: Rather than using prespecified evaluations, we now require an affirmative case that models are sufficiently far from Capability Thresholds.
units.paraphrase: Instead of prespecified evaluations, an affirmative case is now required showing sufficient distance from Capability Thresholds.

units.locator: Changelog / RSP v2.0 / Testing for Capability Thresholds
units.excerpt: Predefined tests may miss emerging risks or be overly conservative relative to the actual threshold of concern.
units.paraphrase: Fixed tests risk missing new risks or being too conservative relative to the real threshold.

units.locator: Changelog / RSP v2.0 / Testing for Capability Thresholds
units.excerpt: Our most accurate tests change frequently enough that it is more practical to use this new approach than to have our Board pre-approve evaluations.
units.paraphrase: Because tests change often, this new approach is more practical than Board pre-approval of evaluations.

units.locator: Changelog / RSP v2.0 / Adjusted evaluation cadence
units.excerpt: Adjusted evaluation cadence: We adjusted the comprehensive assessment cadence to 4x Effective Compute or six months of accumulated post-training enhancements (this was previously three months).
units.paraphrase: The comprehensive assessment cadence was changed to 4x Effective Compute or six months of post-training enhancements, up from three months.

units.locator: Changelog / RSP v2.0 / Adjusted evaluation cadence
units.excerpt: We found that a three-month cadence forced teams to prioritize conducting frequent evaluations over more comprehensive testing and improving methodologies.
units.paraphrase: The prior three-month cadence caused teams to favor frequency over comprehensiveness and methodological improvement.

units.locator: Changelog / RSP v2.0 / Less prescriptive evaluation methodology
units.excerpt: Less prescriptive evaluation methodology: We have replaced some specifics in our previous testing methodology (e.g., using 1% of compute for elicitation or creating a 6x buffer), with more general requirements to (a) match expected efforts of potential adversaries and (b) provide informal estimates of how further scaling and research developments will impact model capabilities and performance on the same tasks.
units.paraphrase: Specific prior methodology details like 1% compute for elicitation or a 6x buffer were replaced with general requirements to match adversary efforts and estimate future scaling impacts.

units.locator: Changelog / RSP v2.0 / Less prescriptive evaluation methodology
units.excerpt: We have found that specific methodologies may become outdated when new research developments are introduced.
units.paraphrase: Specific methodologies risk becoming outdated as new research emerges.

units.locator: Changelog / RSP v2.0 / Less prescriptive evaluation methodology
units.excerpt: Although still an aspirational goal, the science of evaluations is not currently mature enough to make confident predictions about the precise buffer we should require between current models and a Capability Threshold.
units.paraphrase: Precise buffer prediction remains aspirational because evaluation science is not yet mature enough for confident estimates.

units.locator: Changelog / RSP v2.0 / More outcome-focused safeguard requirements
units.excerpt: More outcome-focused safeguard requirements: We have updated our ASL-3 safeguards requirements to be less prescriptive and more outcome-focused.
units.paraphrase: ASL-3 safeguard requirements were made less prescriptive and more focused on outcomes.

units.locator: Changelog / RSP v2.0 / More outcome-focused safeguard requirements
units.excerpt: Rather than detailing specific operational and technical safeguards, we now specify the overall security or deployment standards and requirements for meeting them.
units.paraphrase: Instead of detailed specific safeguards, overall security/deployment standards and their requirements are now specified.

units.locator: Changelog / RSP v2.0 / More outcome-focused safeguard requirements
units.excerpt: This is to allow us to adapt our safeguards more flexibly as our understanding of risks and possible safeguards improves.
units.paraphrase: The change permits more flexible adaptation of safeguards as risk understanding improves.

units.locator: Changelog / RSP v2.0 / Clarified ASL-3 and ASL-2 security threat models
units.excerpt: Clarified ASL-3 and ASL-2 security threat models: We have clarified which actors are in and out of scope for the ASL-3 Security Standard.
units.paraphrase: The scope of actors relevant to the ASL-3 Security Standard was clarified.

units.locator: Changelog / RSP v2.0 / Clarified ASL-3 and ASL-2 security threat models
units.context_stem: Clarified ASL-3 and ASL-2 security threat models.
units.excerpt: We also removed the commitment to protect against scaled attacks and distillation attacks from the ASL-2 Security standard.
units.paraphrase: The ASL-2 Security standard no longer commits to protecting against scaled attacks and distillation attacks.

units.locator: Changelog / RSP v2.0 / Clarified ASL-3 and ASL-2 security threat models
units.context_stem: Clarified ASL-3 and ASL-2 security threat models.
units.excerpt: While distillation remains a concern for more capable models, models stored under ASL-2 safeguards have not yet reached potentially harmful Capability Thresholds.
units.paraphrase: Distillation is still a concern for more capable models, but ASL-2-safeguarded models have not reached harmful Capability Thresholds.

units.locator: Changelog / RSP v2.0 / Clarified requirements for deployments with trusted users
units.excerpt: Clarified requirements for deployments with trusted users: We have updated the ASL-3 Deployment Standard to allow for different levels of safeguards based on deployment context.
units.paraphrase: The ASL-3 Deployment Standard now permits differing safeguard levels depending on deployment context.

units.locator: Changelog / RSP v2.0 / Clarified requirements for deployments with trusted users
units.context_stem: Clarified requirements for deployments with trusted users.
units.excerpt: For any general access systems, we still require passing intensive red-teaming.
units.paraphrase: General access systems still require passing intensive red-teaming.

units.locator: Changelog / RSP v2.0 / Clarified requirements for deployments with trusted users
units.context_stem: Clarified requirements for deployments with trusted users.
units.excerpt: For internal use, safety testing and deployments to sufficiently trusted users, we will instead require a combination of access controls and monitoring.
units.paraphrase: For internal use, testing, and trusted-user deployments, a combination of access controls and monitoring is required instead.

units.locator: Changelog / RSP v2.0 / New Capability and Safeguards Reports
units.excerpt: New Capability and Safeguards Reports: We have introduced Capability Reports and Safeguard Reports.
units.paraphrase: Capability Reports and Safeguard Reports were introduced as new report types.

units.locator: Changelog / RSP v2.0 / New Capability and Safeguards Reports
units.excerpt: We expect that aggregating all the available evidence about model capabilities will provide decision makers with a more complete picture of the overall level of risk and improve our ability to solicit feedback on our work.
units.paraphrase: Aggregating capability evidence is expected to give decision-makers a fuller risk picture and improve feedback solicitation.

units.locator: Changelog / RSP v2.0 / Internal and external accountability
units.excerpt: Internal and external accountability: We have made a number of changes to our previous "procedural commitments." These include expanding the duties of the Responsible Scaling Officer;
units.paraphrase: Several changes were made to procedural commitments, including expanding RSO duties.

units.locator: Changelog / RSP v2.0 / Internal and external accountability
units.excerpt: adding internal critique and external expert input on capability and safeguard assessments; new procedures related to internal governance; and maintaining a public page for overviews of past Capability and Safeguard Reports, RSP-related updates, and future plans.
units.paraphrase: Additional changes added internal critique and external expert input, new internal governance procedures, and a public page for past reports and updates.

units.excerpt: RSP-2025: This update clarifies which Capability Thresholds would require enhanced safeguards beyond our current ASL-3 standards.
units.paraphrase: The v2.1 update clarifies which Capability Thresholds trigger safeguards beyond ASL-3.

units.excerpt: The key changes include:
units.paraphrase: A list of key changes follows.

units.locator: Changelog / RSP v2.1 / New Capability Thresholds
units.excerpt: New Capability Thresholds: We have added a new capability threshold related to CBRN development, which defines capabilities that could substantially uplift the development capabilities of moderately resourced state programs.
units.paraphrase: A new CBRN-related capability threshold was added, defining capabilities that could substantially uplift moderately resourced state programs.

units.locator: Changelog / RSP v2.1 / New Capability Thresholds
units.excerpt: We have also disaggregated our existing AI R&D capability thresholds, separating them into two distinct levels (the ability to fully automate entry-level AI research work, and the ability to cause dramatic acceleration in the rate of effective scaling) and provided additional detail on the corresponding Required Safeguards.
units.paraphrase: The AI R&D thresholds were split into two levels—automating entry-level research and dramatically accelerating effective scaling—with more detail on corresponding safeguards.

units.excerpt: Iterative Commitment: We have adopted a general commitment to reevaluate our Capability Thresholds whenever we upgrade to a new set of Required Safeguards.
units.paraphrase: Anthropic commits to reevaluating Capability Thresholds each time it upgrades Required Safeguards.

units.excerpt: We have decided not to maintain a commitment to define ASL-N+1 evaluations by the time we develop ASL-N models; such an approach would add unnecessary complexity because Capability Thresholds do not naturally come grouped in discrete levels.
units.paraphrase: Anthropic dropped the commitment to predefine next-level evaluations before reaching the current level, since thresholds do not naturally group discretely.

units.excerpt: We believe it is more practical and sensible instead to commit to reconsidering the whole list of Capability Thresholds whenever we upgrade our safeguards.
units.paraphrase: Reconsidering the entire list of Capability Thresholds at each safeguard upgrade is deemed more practical.

units.excerpt: ASL-3 Security: This update excludes both sophisticated insiders and state-compromised insiders from the ASL-3 Security Standard.
units.paraphrase: The v2.2 update excludes both sophisticated insiders and state-compromised insiders from the ASL-3 Security Standard.

units.excerpt: Previously, only "highly sophisticated state-compromised insiders" were explicitly excluded.
units.paraphrase: The prior exclusion covered only highly sophisticated state-compromised insiders.

units.excerpt: The model capabilities and threat models corresponding with the ASL-3 Security Standard do not warrant protection against either group: the CBRN-3 threat models entail large numbers of users having access to unguarded models (which is more likely to occur through a universal jailbreak than via model theft), and the relatively small number of employees who might be capable of model theft does not significantly affect the risk level.
units.paraphrase: Neither insider group needs protection under ASL-3, since CBRN-3 threats center on universal jailbreaks over model theft, and few employees could execute model theft anyway.

units.excerpt: For AI R&D-4, the threat models generally do not depend on model weight theft and instead entail AI systems engaging in autonomous internal sabotage.
units.paraphrase: For AI R&D-4, threat models center on autonomous internal sabotage rather than weight theft.

units.excerpt: This update is a comprehensive rewrite of our RSP. For a summary of changes and the thinking behind them, see here.
units.paraphrase: The v3.0 update is a full rewrite of the RSP, with a separate summary of changes referenced.

units.excerpt: This revision addresses the following points: (1) how we operationalize the Automated R&D capability threshold; (2) how we use internal feedback on Risk Reports; and (3) that we may consider pausing development or deployment even where the commitments described in Appendix A are not triggered.
units.paraphrase: The v3.1 revision covers operationalizing the Automated R&D threshold, using internal feedback on Risk Reports, and considering pauses even without Appendix A triggers.

units.excerpt: These changes are mostly clarificatory in nature; we don't see them as significant changes to substance.
units.paraphrase: The v3.1 changes are characterized as mostly clarificatory rather than substantive.

units.excerpt: Change (1) reflects further discussion of our operationalization of the capability threshold, and involves some substantive changes to make it better reflect our underlying intent.
units.paraphrase: Change (1) involves substantive changes to better reflect the intended meaning of the capability threshold.

units.excerpt: This update also includes minor edits for style or clarity.
units.paraphrase: The update also contains minor stylistic or clarity edits.

units.excerpt: This and other italicized instances of "highly capable" use the term as defined in Section 3.6.
units.paraphrase: A footnote clarifies that italicized uses of 'highly capable' follow the Section 3.6 definition.

excerpt: Our Responsible Scaling Policy (RSP) is our voluntary framework for managing catastrophic risks from advanced AI systems.
paraphrase: The RSP is described as Anthropic's voluntary framework for managing catastrophic AI risks.

excerpt: It establishes how we identify and evaluate risks, how we make decisions about AI development and deployment, and, from the perspective of the world at large, how we aim to make sure that the benefits of our models exceed their costs.
paraphrase: The RSP sets out how risks are identified, how development and deployment decisions are made, and how benefits are ensured to outweigh costs.

excerpt: We have always intended for our RSP to be a living document.
paraphrase: Anthropic states the RSP has always been intended as a living document.

excerpt: We will continually update the RSP as we learn more about AI capabilities and risks, develop and refine technical safety measures, and gain more experience navigating an ecosystem in which the risks to society depend on the actions of many developers.
paraphrase: Anthropic commits to continually updating the RSP as understanding of capabilities, risks, safety measures, and the multi-developer ecosystem grows.

excerpt: The major components of this third iteration are as follows:
paraphrase: This sentence introduces the list of major components of the third RSP iteration.

excerpt: Our recommendations for industry-wide safety outline what it would take, at an industry-wide level, to keep catastrophic risks reliably low through a period of rapid advances in AI capabilities.
paraphrase: The document describes industry-wide recommendations for keeping catastrophic risk low during rapid AI advancement.

excerpt: We lay this out in a table that maps capability thresholds to the mitigations we believe they call for.
paraphrase: A table maps capability thresholds to corresponding mitigations.

excerpt: We also include our planned mitigations as a company, which are drawn from other sections of this policy and associated artifacts.
paraphrase: The table also includes company-specific planned mitigations sourced from other parts of the policy.

excerpt: This approach represents a change from our previous RSP, driven by a collective action problem.
paraphrase: The new approach is explained as a change from the prior RSP due to a collective action problem.

excerpt: The overall level of catastrophic risk from AI depends on the actions of multiple AI developers, not just one.
paraphrase: Catastrophic AI risk depends on the collective actions of multiple developers.

excerpt: Our previous RSP committed to implementing mitigations that would reduce our models' absolute risk levels to acceptable levels, without regard to whether other frontier AI developers would do the same.
paraphrase: The prior RSP committed to reducing absolute risk regardless of other developers' actions.

excerpt: But from a societal perspective, what matters is the risk to the ecosystem as a whole.
paraphrase: From society's viewpoint, the relevant risk is that of the whole ecosystem, not a single developer.

excerpt: If one AI developer paused development to implement safety measures while others moved forward with training and deploying AI systems without strong mitigations, that could result in a world that is less safe—the developers with the weakest protections would set the pace, and responsible developers would lose their ability to do safety research and advance the public benefit.
paraphrase: Unilateral pausing by one developer while others proceed unsafely could make the world less safe overall, ceding pace-setting to the least protective actors.

excerpt: Although this situation has not yet arisen, it looks likely enough that we want to prepare for it.
paraphrase: This collective action problem has not yet materialized but is likely enough to warrant preparation.

excerpt: We now separate our plans as a company—those which we expect to achieve regardless of what any other company does—from our more ambitious industry-wide recommendations.
paraphrase: Anthropic now distinguishes its own company commitments from broader, more ambitious industry-wide recommendations.

excerpt: We aspire to advance the latter through a mixture of example-setting, addressing unsolved technical problems, advocacy through industry groups, and policy advocacy.
paraphrase: Anthropic aims to advance industry-wide recommendations via example-setting, technical work, industry advocacy, and policy advocacy.

excerpt: But we cannot commit to following them unilaterally.
paraphrase: Anthropic states it cannot unilaterally commit to the industry-wide recommendations.

excerpt: Frontier Safety Roadmaps are a new requirement under our RSP.
paraphrase: Frontier Safety Roadmaps are introduced as a new RSP requirement.

excerpt: These will describe our concrete plans for making progress across Security, Alignment, Safeguards, and Policy.
paraphrase: The Roadmaps will detail plans for progress in Security, Alignment, Safeguards, and Policy.

excerpt: Goals described in the Roadmaps are intended to be ambitious, yet achievable—providing the kind of forcing function that we consider to be a past success of our RSP.
paraphrase: Roadmap goals are meant to be ambitious yet achievable, functioning as a forcing mechanism similar to past RSP successes.

excerpt: These are not hard commitments but rather public goals against which we will openly grade our progress.
paraphrase: Roadmap goals are not binding commitments but public benchmarks for openly tracking progress.

excerpt: Risk Reports are another new requirement.
paraphrase: Risk Reports are introduced as another new RSP requirement.

excerpt: Risk Reports will provide detailed information on the safety profile of our models at the time of publication.
paraphrase: Risk Reports will detail the safety profile of models as of publication.

excerpt: They will go beyond describing model capabilities, addressing our thinking on how capabilities, threat models (the specific ways that models might pose threats), and active risk mitigations fit together, providing an assessment of the overall level of risk.
paraphrase: Risk Reports will integrate capabilities, threat models, and mitigations into an overall risk assessment, beyond just describing capabilities.

excerpt: These reports will reflect our reasoning as to whether we believe the risks of training or deploying our models are justified by their corresponding benefits to the world.
paraphrase: Risk Reports will explain whether the risks of training/deploying models are justified by their benefits.

excerpt: They will be published online, with some redactions to protect sensitive details about, for example, our training methods and organizations with whom we work.
paraphrase: Risk Reports will be published online with redactions to protect sensitive information such as training methods and partner organizations.

excerpt: As detailed below, we also aim to subject Risk Reports to review by credible, independent external parties.
paraphrase: Anthropic aims to have Risk Reports reviewed by credible independent external parties.

excerpt: Finally, our governance commitments are intended to promote internal and external accountability, similar to those in our previous RSP.
paraphrase: Governance commitments continue to aim at internal and external accountability, similar to the prior RSP.

excerpt: Our RSP is only one part of our overall approach to safety.
paraphrase: The RSP is only one component of Anthropic's broader safety approach.

excerpt: For instance, although this policy focuses on catastrophic risks, they are not the only risks we consider important—our Usage Policy and societal impacts research address other concerns.
paraphrase: Other risks beyond catastrophic ones are addressed by the Usage Policy and societal impacts research.

excerpt: Further, the RSP may serve some regulatory requirements, but it is not designed to be comprehensive.
paraphrase: The RSP may partially satisfy regulatory requirements but is not intended to be comprehensive regulatory compliance.

excerpt: We want to keep it focused on our most central measures for addressing the catastrophic risks we prioritize most, rather than expand it to address every obligation we face.
paraphrase: The RSP is deliberately kept focused on core catastrophic-risk measures rather than every obligation.

excerpt: Where regulatory requirements exceed or differ from what the RSP covers, we will address them through separate documents.
paraphrase: Additional or differing regulatory requirements will be handled in separate documents.

excerpt: "Catastrophic risk" as used in our RSP refers generally to risks of the most severe potential harms from advanced AI, such as existential threats or fundamental destabilization of global systems.
paraphrase: Footnote defines catastrophic risk as the most severe potential AI harms, such as existential threats or global destabilization.

excerpt: We use this term in its plain meaning rather than adopting any specific statutory definition.
paraphrase: The term catastrophic risk is used in its plain meaning, not a statutory definition.

excerpt: Where laws such as California SB 53 define this or similar terms with specific thresholds, we address those requirements in separate compliance frameworks.
paraphrase: Statutory definitions such as California SB 53's are handled through separate compliance frameworks.

excerpt: This section outlines our recommendations for what it would take, at an industry-wide level, to keep catastrophic risks reliably low through a period of rapid advances in AI capabilities.
paraphrase: This section presents recommendations for industry-wide measures to keep catastrophic risk low amid rapid AI progress.

excerpt: We lay this out in a three-column table.
paraphrase: The recommendations are presented in a three-column table.

excerpt: The left column identifies capability thresholds that would call for heightened mitigations.
paraphrase: The left column of the table lists capability thresholds requiring heightened mitigations.

excerpt: The middle column provides an overview of our planned mitigations, which we have set forth more fully in our Frontier Safety Roadmap and other sections of this policy.
paraphrase: The middle column summarizes planned mitigations detailed further in the Roadmap and elsewhere in the policy.

excerpt: The right column describes our recommendations for industry-wide safety at each threshold.
paraphrase: The right column contains the industry-wide safety recommendations for each threshold.

excerpt: The distinction between our plans as a company (middle column) and our industry-wide recommendations (right column) reflects the limitations of any single AI developer's ability to ensure safety across the industry.
paraphrase: The company/industry-wide distinction reflects that a single developer cannot ensure industry-wide safety alone.

excerpt: In particular, we cannot unilaterally and unconditionally commit to staying in line with the industry-wide recommendations in the right column.
paraphrase: Anthropic cannot unilaterally and unconditionally commit to the industry-wide recommendations.

excerpt: However, these recommendations will drive important aspects of our work:
paraphrase: The recommendations will nonetheless shape important aspects of Anthropic's work, as detailed below.

context_stem: However, these recommendations will drive important aspects of our work:
excerpt: We use these recommendations as the north star for our risk mitigations planning as well as our public policy work.
paraphrase: The recommendations serve as the guiding standard for risk mitigation planning and public policy work.

context_stem: However, these recommendations will drive important aspects of our work:
excerpt: We will strive to advance these recommendations through a mixture of example-setting, addressing unsolved technical problems, advocacy through industry groups, and policy advocacy.
paraphrase: Anthropic will try to advance these recommendations through example-setting, technical work, industry advocacy, and policy advocacy.

context_stem: However, these recommendations will drive important aspects of our work:
excerpt: We have also adopted a set of competitor-contingent commitments (see Appendix A) aimed at staying in line with these recommendations in scenarios where we can be confident that other relevant AI developers are doing the same.
paraphrase: Anthropic has adopted competitor-contingent commitments to follow the recommendations when confident other developers do likewise.

excerpt: At this point in AI's rapid development, we cannot presently give highly specific advance detail on what evaluations will determine whether risk thresholds have been passed, or what risk mitigations will be needed to achieve safety.
paraphrase: Anthropic cannot currently specify in detail the evaluations for passing risk thresholds or the mitigations needed.

excerpt: Our recommendations for industry-wide safety are thus structured around requiring analysis and arguments making a strong case for safety, rather than AI Safety Levels (more in Appendix B).
paraphrase: The recommendations rely on requiring safety-case analysis and argument rather than fixed AI Safety Levels.

excerpt: This leaves flexibility in how risk thresholds are evaluated and how safety is achieved and argued for.
paraphrase: This structure allows flexibility in threshold evaluation and safety argumentation.

excerpt: But it creates a challenge: one actor's view of what constitutes good risk assessment and mitigation may be very different from another's.
paraphrase: This flexibility creates a challenge because views on adequate risk assessment and mitigation may differ across actors.

excerpt: Ultimately, the best way for these recommendations to be implemented is likely via governance of all relevant frontier AI developers by third parties that determine which developers need to provide risk analyses and make arguments for the safety of their systems, and determine which such arguments are adequate.
paraphrase: Anthropic suggests third-party governance of all frontier developers as the best implementation path, determining who must provide risk analyses and judging their adequacy.

excerpt: To the extent this takes the form of national regulation, different countries should attempt to harmonize their governance, including standards of evidence, to avoid a race to the bottom.
paraphrase: Countries should harmonize national regulation and evidentiary standards to avoid a race to the bottom.

excerpt: In the shorter run, independent bodies (standards-setting organizations, auditors, etc.) might review such arguments and enforce high quality standards for private AI developers via voluntary mechanisms.
paraphrase: In the near term, independent bodies could voluntarily review and enforce quality standards for private AI developers.

excerpt: Note that an AI developer might provide a single analysis covering a broad category of models, such that there isn't a new analysis needed for each release.
paraphrase: A single analysis could cover a broad model category rather than requiring per-release analyses.

excerpt: Additionally, determinations of which AI developers need to provide such analysis should be made with an effort to spare smaller AI developers from unnecessary compliance burden.
paraphrase: Determinations of which developers must provide analysis should try to spare smaller developers unnecessary compliance burden.

excerpt: We expect that the recommendations for industry-wide safety will evolve significantly, as we learn more about AI capabilities, threat models, and risk mitigations.
paraphrase: The industry-wide recommendations are expected to evolve significantly as knowledge improves.

excerpt: We hope these recommendations will become increasingly specific over time.
paraphrase: Anthropic hopes the recommendations become more specific over time.

paraphrase: Frontier developers should argue convincingly that threat actors won't gain significantly increased ability to cause the described catastrophic harm.

excerpt: This will likely require similar measures to those from the previous row, but to a higher standard—to the point where even well-resourced and -staffed threat actors would be unlikely to reliably jailbreak models or cause catastrophic harm via unauthorized access to or modification of models (including via stolen or modified model weights).
paraphrase: Similar but stronger measures than the prior row are needed, sufficient to resist even well-resourced threat actors from jailbreaking or misusing stolen/modified weights.

paraphrase: This implies security roughly at RAND SL4, contingent on the capabilities of the strongest plausible unbound threat actors.

paraphrase: This threshold covers AI systems highly relied upon with sensitive access and moderate autonomous/subterfuge capacity, plausibly able to cause sabotage that raises catastrophe odds irreversibly.

paraphrase: Longer term, this threshold could extend to AI systems deployed in government and other high-stakes settings.

context_stem: Row: Automated R&D in key domains. Column: Capability or usage threshold.
excerpt: We will consider this threshold to be met if we determine that either (1) our models would be able to fully substitute for our entire set of Research Scientists and Research Engineers, at competitive costs (i.e., within a factor of 5); or (2) there is "dramatic acceleration" of the pace of AI progress for reasons that likely relate to the automation of AI R&D.
paraphrase: The threshold is met if models could fully replace all Research Scientists/Engineers at competitive cost (within 5x), or if AI-driven R&D automation causes dramatic acceleration.

locator: Table / Automated R&D in key domains / Capability or usage threshold
context_stem: Row: Automated R&D in key domains. Column: Capability or usage threshold.
excerpt: We would consider scenario (2) to have occurred where (a) we observe or expect double the rate of progress in AI aggregate capabilities compared to the rate we'd expect in the absence of significant AI contributions to AI R&D and (b) it is plausible that this doubling is substantially attributable to the automation of research and/or engineering (as opposed to other factors, such as increased headcount, compute, or general productivity), such that continuation of the trend in AI progress could lead to even greater acceleration.
paraphrase: Scenario (2) requires observing double the expected AI capability progress rate attributable substantially to R&D automation rather than other factors, with potential for further acceleration.

excerpt: We will comprehensively gather, centralize, and maintain logs for all critical AI-development activities, and use AI to analyze them for issues including security threats, concerning behavior by insiders (humans as well as AI systems themselves), and training processes or data that are out of line with the public Constitution that shapes and defines our AI models.
paraphrase: Anthropic will comprehensively log critical AI-development activities and use AI to analyze them for security threats, insider concerns (human or AI), and misalignment with the public Constitution.

locator: Table / Automated R&D in key domains / Mitigations—our plan as a company / bullet 3
context_stem: Row: Automated R&D in key domains. Column: Mitigations—our plan as a company. We will:
excerpt: Perform systematic alignment assessments to examine Claude's behavioral patterns and propensities, meaningfully incorporating mechanistic interpretability and adversarial red-teaming to test our auditing methods.
paraphrase: Anthropic will conduct systematic alignment assessments of Claude's behavior using mechanistic interpretability and adversarial red-teaming.

locator: Table / Automated R&D in key domains / Mitigations—our plan as a company / bullet 4
context_stem: Row: Automated R&D in key domains. Column: Mitigations—our plan as a company. We will:
excerpt: Develop our internal red-teaming of our deployment safeguards to the point where our internal red-teaming performs better at finding potential jailbreaks than the collective abilities of the participants in our established bug bounty programs.
paraphrase: Anthropic will strengthen internal red-teaming until it outperforms the combined efforts of its bug bounty program participants at finding jailbreaks.

locator: Table / Automated R&D in key domains / Mitigations—our plan as a company / bullet 5
context_stem: Row: Automated R&D in key domains. Column: Mitigations—our plan as a company. We will:
excerpt: Publish Risk Reports with the status of, and noteworthy findings from, all of the above, subject to external review by at least one expert, experienced, credible, candid and disinterested external party.
paraphrase: Anthropic will publish Risk Reports on the status/findings of these efforts, subject to review by at least one qualified independent external party.

locator: Table / Automated R&D in key domains / Mitigations—our plan as a company
context_stem: Row: Automated R&D in key domains. Column: Mitigations—our plan as a company.
excerpt: We broadly expect to lead the industry in practices that reduce the risks from AI, although we cannot unilaterally make guarantees about the safety level of AI this advanced.
paraphrase: Anthropic expects to lead the industry in risk-reducing practices but cannot unilaterally guarantee safety at this advanced capability level.
