context_stem: Row: Automated R&D in key domains. Column: Mitigations—ambitious industry-wide recommendations.
excerpt: A frontier developer should make a strong argument that:
paraphrase: Lead-in to a list of arguments frontier developers should make for this threshold.

locator: Table / Automated R&D in key domains / Mitigations—ambitious industry-wide recommendations / bullet 1
context_stem: Row: Automated R&D in key domains. Column: Mitigations—ambitious industry-wide recommendations. A frontier developer should make a strong argument that:
excerpt: No user or team of users (including those backed by top-tier states) will become significantly more likely to cause catastrophic harm via their usage of product surfaces or via theft of model weights.
paraphrase: Recommended argument: no user or team, even state-backed, gains significantly increased ability to cause catastrophic harm via product use or weight theft.

locator: Table / Automated R&D in key domains / Mitigations—ambitious industry-wide recommendations / bullet 1
context_stem: Row: Automated R&D in key domains. Column: Mitigations—ambitious industry-wide recommendations. A frontier developer should make a strong argument that:
excerpt: This will likely require similar measures to those listed in row 1, but to a higher standard‚ to the point where even well-resourced and -staffed threat actors would be unlikely to reliably jailbreak models or cause catastrophic harm via unauthorized access to or modification of models (including via stolen or modified model weights).
paraphrase: This requires row-1-type measures at a higher standard sufficient to resist well-resourced threat actors from jailbreaking or misusing stolen/modified weights.

locator: Table / Automated R&D in key domains / Mitigations—ambitious industry-wide recommendations / bullet 1
context_stem: Row: Automated R&D in key domains. Column: Mitigations—ambitious industry-wide recommendations. A frontier developer should make a strong argument that:
excerpt: Accomplishing this would likely mean security roughly in line with RAND SL4. Security requirements would be calibrated to defend against the strongest plausible threat actors who are not bound by a credible industry-wide safety regime.
paraphrase: This implies security roughly at RAND SL4, calibrated against the strongest plausible unbound threat actors.

locator: Table / Automated R&D in key domains / Mitigations—ambitious industry-wide recommendations / bullet 1
context_stem: Row: Automated R&D in key domains. Column: Mitigations—ambitious industry-wide recommendations. A frontier developer should make a strong argument that:
excerpt: Actors subject to such a regime would not need to be treated as threats to each other's model weights.
paraphrase: Developers under a credible industry-wide regime would not need to treat each other as weight-theft threats.

locator: Table / Automated R&D in key domains / Mitigations—ambitious industry-wide recommendations / bullet 2
context_stem: Row: Automated R&D in key domains. Column: Mitigations—ambitious industry-wide recommendations. A frontier developer should make a strong argument that:
excerpt: Even malicious employees and other insiders with maximal levels of access will not be significantly enabled to cause catastrophic harm.
paraphrase: Recommended argument: even maximally privileged malicious insiders would not be significantly enabled to cause catastrophic harm.

locator: Table / Automated R&D in key domains / Mitigations—ambitious industry-wide recommendations / bullet 2
context_stem: Row: Automated R&D in key domains. Column: Mitigations—ambitious industry-wide recommendations. A frontier developer should make a strong argument that:
excerpt: This requires (among other things) accounting for internal tools that are less restricted than product surfaces, and for the possibility of unauthorized modification of models.
paraphrase: This requires accounting for less-restricted internal tools and the possibility of unauthorized model modification.

locator: Table / Automated R&D in key domains / Mitigations—ambitious industry-wide recommendations / bullet 2
context_stem: Row: Automated R&D in key domains. Column: Mitigations—ambitious industry-wide recommendations. A frontier developer should make a strong argument that:
excerpt: This will likely require an internal Usage Policy and strong internal compartmentalization, controls and/or monitoring to restrict the ability of employees and contractors (up to and including the company's CEO as well as its most privileged technical employees) to circumvent the Usage Policy.
paraphrase: This likely requires an internal Usage Policy plus strong compartmentalization/controls/monitoring restricting even the CEO and top technical staff from circumventing it.

locator: Table / Automated R&D in key domains / Mitigations—ambitious industry-wide recommendations / bullet 3
context_stem: Row: Automated R&D in key domains. Column: Mitigations—ambitious industry-wide recommendations. A frontier developer should make a strong argument that:
excerpt: AI models have not been deliberately or inadvertently trained with dangerous goals, or are otherwise unlikely to autonomously cause catastrophic harm.
paraphrase: Recommended argument: models have not been trained (deliberately or inadvertently) with dangerous goals and are unlikely to autonomously cause catastrophic harm.

locator: Table / Automated R&D in key domains / Mitigations—ambitious industry-wide recommendations / bullet 3
context_stem: Row: Automated R&D in key domains. Column: Mitigations—ambitious industry-wide recommendations. A frontier developer should make a strong argument that:
excerpt: This will likely require similar measures to those listed above under "High-stakes sabotage opportunities" (some combination of internal compartmentalization, restriction and code review; monitoring AI behavior; and evidence that AI models lack the propensity to deceive and manipulate users), but to a greater degree.
paraphrase: This requires similar but stronger measures to those under high-stakes sabotage: compartmentalization, monitoring, and evidence against deceptive/manipulative propensities.

locator: Table / Automated R&D in key domains / Mitigations—ambitious industry-wide recommendations / bullet 3
context_stem: Row: Automated R&D in key domains. Column: Mitigations—ambitious industry-wide recommendations. A frontier developer should make a strong argument that:
excerpt: In particular, at this point AI systems might be responsible for much of the research and analysis that underpins risk assessment, and might have strong capabilities for deception, manipulation and obfuscation of evidence, in which case analyses of threats from AIs should follow very high evidentiary standards with thorough and careful analysis of the possibility that much of the key evidence is suspect due to the possibility of manipulation by AI systems.
paraphrase: Because AI may generate much of the risk-assessment evidence and could be capable of deception/manipulation, threat analyses should apply very high evidentiary standards accounting for possible evidence manipulation.

excerpt: We will maintain a Frontier Safety Roadmap laying out ambitious but achievable goals for improving our risk mitigations—charting our progress as a company and raising the bar over time.
paraphrase: Anthropic will maintain a Frontier Safety Roadmap with ambitious, achievable goals that track and raise the bar on risk mitigation progress.

excerpt: Maintaining and reporting on this Roadmap is part of our work under the RSP.
paraphrase: Roadmap maintenance and reporting are part of the RSP's obligations.

excerpt: It will be shared with all full-time employees as well as our Board of Directors (Board) and Long-Term Benefit Trust (LTBT), and published in redacted form.
paraphrase: The Roadmap will be shared internally with all full-time employees, the Board, and the LTBT, and published externally in redacted form.

excerpt: We will provide updates on whether we achieve the goals, and set new goals when we do.
paraphrase: Anthropic will report on goal achievement and set new goals as achieved.

excerpt: Our Frontier Safety Roadmap is subject to change.
paraphrase: The Roadmap can change over time.

excerpt: Some changes may simply reflect our evolving understanding of how best to mitigate key risks.
paraphrase: Changes to the Roadmap may reflect evolving understanding of risk mitigation.

excerpt: However, we will strive to avoid situations where we revise the goals in a less ambitious direction simply because we are unable to achieve them.
paraphrase: Anthropic will try to avoid weakening Roadmap goals merely due to an inability to meet them.

excerpt: By establishing this expectation, we hope to create a forcing function for work that would otherwise be challenging to appropriately prioritize and resource, as it requires collaboration (and in some cases sacrifices) from multiple parts of the company and can be at cross-purposes with immediate competitive and commercial priorities.
paraphrase: This expectation is meant to force prioritization of cross-company collaborative work that might otherwise conflict with competitive/commercial priorities.

excerpt: Publishing our Frontier Safety Roadmap may also help inform broader industry and policy discussions on AI safety.
paraphrase: Publishing the Roadmap may also contribute to broader industry and policy discussions on AI safety.

excerpt: Our current Frontier Safety Roadmap is available at anthropic.com/responsible-scaling-policy/roadmap.
paraphrase: The current Roadmap is published at a specified Anthropic URL.

excerpt: We will also keep past Roadmaps available at that link.
paraphrase: Past versions of the Roadmap will remain accessible at the same link.

excerpt: We will publish Risk Reports discussing the risks of our systems and how we have made determinations about whether to continue AI development and deployment in light of the risks.
paraphrase: Anthropic will publish Risk Reports that discuss system risks and the determinations made about continuing development and deployment.

excerpt: These have significant content in common with system cards, but we are adding additional structure and process aimed at presenting our overall assessments of risk.
paraphrase: Risk Reports overlap substantially with system cards but add structure and process for presenting overall risk assessments.

excerpt: Scope. A Risk Report will cover all publicly deployed models at the time of its publication.
paraphrase: A Risk Report's scope includes all models publicly deployed at the time of publication.

excerpt: It will also cover internally deployed models when we determine that these models could pose significant risks5 beyond those posed by models that are covered by a prior Risk Report.
paraphrase: Internally deployed models are also covered if determined to pose significant risks beyond previously covered models.

excerpt: While there are a variety of reasons we might classify an internal model this way, this will—at a minimum—include any internal models that we are deploying for large-scale, fully autonomous research.
paraphrase: At minimum, internal models used for large-scale, fully autonomous research will be classified as posing significant risk.

excerpt: Models fitting the above description are abbreviated below as "in-scope models."
paraphrase: Models meeting the scope description are termed "in-scope models."

excerpt: We may also voluntarily include additional models in a Risk Report, e.g., to contribute to general discourse, but such inclusion does not expand the commitments below.
paraphrase: Additional models may be voluntarily included for discourse purposes without expanding the stated commitments.

excerpt: Timing. We will publish a Risk Report every 3-6 months.
paraphrase: Risk Reports will be published on a 3-6 month cadence.

excerpt: Note that unlike system cards, Risk Reports will not be published with each new model release.
paraphrase: Risk Reports differ from system cards in that they are not tied to every model release.

excerpt: When we publicly deploy a model that we determine is significantly more capable than any of the models covered in the most recent Risk Report, we will publish a discussion (in our System Card or elsewhere) of how that model's capabilities and propensities affect or change the analysis in the Risk Report.
paraphrase: If a newly deployed public model is significantly more capable than those in the latest Risk Report, a discussion of its impact on the analysis will be published.

excerpt: Within 30 days of determining that we have an internally deployed model that is in-scope (per the description above), we will publish a discussion (in a System Card or elsewhere) of how that model's capabilities and propensities affect or change the analysis in the Risk Report.
paraphrase: Within 30 days of identifying an in-scope internally deployed model, a discussion of its effect on the Risk Report analysis will be published.

excerpt: Specifically, risks arising from the capability thresholds in our recommendations for industry-wide safety (see Section 1).
paraphrase: Footnote clarifies that significant risks refer to those from capability thresholds in the industry-wide safety recommendations.

excerpt: Several principles guide how we approach Risk Reports:
paraphrase: The section introduces guiding principles for Risk Reports.

context_stem: Several principles guide how we approach Risk Reports:
excerpt: We intend for our Risk Reports to be direct, candid, and informative about how we see the risks of our systems and our state of preparedness for them.
paraphrase: Risk Reports are intended to be direct, candid, and informative about system risks and preparedness.

context_stem: Several principles guide how we approach Risk Reports:
excerpt: In particular, we will acknowledge when we view certain models as posing significant risks in absolute terms, even if our marginal contribution to overall ecosystem risk may be relatively limited when taking other developers' AI models into account.
paraphrase: Anthropic will acknowledge significant absolute risk of its models even if its marginal contribution to ecosystem risk is limited.

context_stem: Several principles guide how we approach Risk Reports:
excerpt: We will put significant effort into investigating (for example, via capability evaluations) the case for risk, and into sharing what we find.
paraphrase: Significant effort will be devoted to investigating risk cases, such as through capability evaluations, and to sharing findings.

context_stem: Several principles guide how we approach Risk Reports:
excerpt: When a Risk Report describes risk mitigations we have in place (or plan to implement shortly), we will keep our future practices in line with this description or track and report noteworthy changes and deviations (generally via subsequent Risk Reports).
paraphrase: Future practices will remain consistent with described mitigations, or noteworthy changes will be tracked and reported in later Risk Reports.

context_stem: When a Risk Report describes risk mitigations we have in place...
excerpt: We should make a strong attempt to ensure that ongoing (as opposed to temporary) changes do not significantly increase the level of risk.
paraphrase: A strong effort should be made to ensure ongoing changes do not significantly raise risk levels.

excerpt: Factual information. We will describe how we identify, evaluate, and mitigate catastrophic risks.
paraphrase: Risk Reports will describe processes for identifying, evaluating, and mitigating catastrophic risks.

excerpt: A Risk Report will document the following:
paraphrase: The Risk Report will document a list of items.

context_stem: A Risk Report will document the following:
excerpt: Threat model identification: Our criteria for determining which catastrophic risks (i.e., threat models) we assess.
paraphrase: The report will document criteria used to determine which catastrophic risk threat models are assessed.

context_stem: A Risk Report will document the following:
excerpt: Threat model specification: The relevant threat models (which will, at a minimum, include those discussed above).
paraphrase: The report will specify relevant threat models, including at minimum those previously discussed.

context_stem: A Risk Report will document the following:
excerpt: Evidence (including evaluations) about relevant model capabilities and behaviors: For each in-scope model, capability and alignment evaluations (conducted internally and by external parties as appropriate), their results, and (as appropriate) other evidence we considered in assessing the level of risk.
paraphrase: For each in-scope model, the report will document capability and alignment evaluation evidence, results, and other risk-relevant evidence.

context_stem: A Risk Report will document the following:
excerpt: Risk mitigations: For each in-scope model, the mitigations we are implementing across security, deployment safeguards, and alignment domains, along with discussion of their effectiveness.
paraphrase: For each in-scope model, the report documents mitigations across security, deployment safeguards, and alignment and their effectiveness.

context_stem: A Risk Report will document the following:
excerpt: Additional relevant factors: Any other considerations material to our risk analysis.
paraphrase: The report will include any other considerations material to the risk analysis.

excerpt: Risk analyses. We will provide our reasoning and conclusions regarding both specific threat models and overall risk levels.
paraphrase: Risk analyses will present reasoning and conclusions about specific threat models and overall risk levels.

excerpt: Our analyses will include:
paraphrase: The analyses will include the following items.

excerpt: Threat-specific risk assessment: For each threat model, we will analyze remaining absolute risk–i.e., the leftover risk after accounting for our mitigations.
paraphrase: For each threat model, remaining absolute risk after mitigations will be analyzed.

context_stem: Our analyses will include: Threat-specific risk assessment...
excerpt: We will also discuss whether we believe we've crossed relevant thresholds in our recommendations for industry-wide safety (see Section 1), and (as relevant) whether we believe we're meeting the risk mitigation standards corresponding to them.
paraphrase: The report will discuss whether relevant safety thresholds have been crossed and whether corresponding mitigation standards are being met.

excerpt: Overall risk assessment: We will provide an overall risk assessment.
paraphrase: An overall risk assessment will be provided.

excerpt: Risk-benefit determination: We will explain whether, and if so why, we believe the identified risks are justified by corresponding benefits.
paraphrase: The report will explain whether and why identified risks are justified by corresponding benefits.

excerpt: Looking forward: We will outline our plans for continuing to monitor and mitigate the relevant risks over time.
paraphrase: Plans for ongoing monitoring and mitigation of relevant risks will be outlined.

excerpt: Review of past Risk Reports and decisions. We will address:
paraphrase: This part of the report addresses review of past Risk Reports and decisions.

context_stem: Review of past Risk Reports and decisions. We will address:
excerpt: Changes in risk mitigation practices—noteworthy cases in which our risk mitigation practices deviated (including temporarily) or changed from what we discussed in our previous Risk Report over the relevant period, and their implications for the overall level of risk.
paraphrase: The report addresses noteworthy deviations or changes in risk mitigation practices since the last Risk Report and their implications for overall risk.

context_stem: Review of past Risk Reports and decisions. We will address:
excerpt: Decisions to internally deploy in-scope models that would not otherwise be reviewed in a Risk Report (because they happened in between Risk Reports).
paraphrase: The report covers internal deployment decisions of in-scope models that occurred between Risk Reports.

context_stem: Decisions to internally deploy in-scope models...
excerpt: We will discuss how these decisions were made and whether they appear reasonable in light of any noteworthy new information that has come to light since then.
paraphrase: The report will discuss how such deployment decisions were made and whether they were reasonable given subsequent new information.

context_stem: Review of past Risk Reports and decisions. We will address:
excerpt: Changes to our Frontier Safety Roadmap and any cases where we failed to meet our goals.
paraphrase: The report addresses changes to the Frontier Safety Roadmap and instances of unmet goals.

excerpt: Marginal risk and ecosystem analysis. If we determine that the absolute level of risk being imposed industry-wide by AI systems such as ours is high, and are justifying our decision to move forward based partly on a marginal risk analysis,6 we will additionally address the following:
paraphrase: If industry-wide absolute risk is determined high and the decision to proceed partly relies on marginal risk analysis, additional items will be addressed.

context_stem: Marginal risk and ecosystem analysis... we will additionally address the following:
excerpt: Competitive landscape analysis: What we know about how our current and future model capabilities and risk mitigations compare to those of relevant competitors.
paraphrase: The additional analysis compares current and future model capabilities and mitigations to competitors.

context_stem: Marginal risk and ecosystem analysis... we will additionally address the following:
excerpt: Role in risk assessment: How these comparisons factored into our risk assessment.
paraphrase: The analysis explains how competitive comparisons factored into the risk assessment.

context_stem: Marginal risk and ecosystem analysis... we will additionally address the following:
excerpt: Benefits analysis: The benefits, if any, of continuing to maintain our existing models or of advancing frontier capabilities, including considerations related to our mission and our ability to contribute to AI safety research and policy development.
paraphrase: The analysis includes benefits of maintaining models or advancing capabilities, including mission-related considerations and safety research contributions.

context_stem: Marginal risk and ecosystem analysis... we will additionally address the following:
excerpt: Advocacy efforts: The steps we took to raise public awareness of the relevant risks and to encourage appropriate regulatory action, including our engagement with policymakers and other AI developers.
paraphrase: The analysis documents steps taken to raise public awareness of risks and encourage regulatory action, including policymaker engagement.

excerpt: We will conduct the assessments above with respect to each in-scope model.
paraphrase: All the described assessments will be conducted for each in-scope model.

excerpt: To avoid redundancy, we will likely analyze similar models collectively rather than individually, with appropriate justification for any such groupings.
paraphrase: Similar models may be analyzed collectively rather than individually, with justification, to avoid redundancy.

excerpt: Initial assessment and drafting: Our internal subject matter experts will conduct risk assessments and draft the Risk Report.
paraphrase: Internal subject matter experts conduct the risk assessments and draft the Risk Report.

excerpt: Review and feedback: We will solicit comprehensive internal feedback on the report, focusing on identifying potential methodological weaknesses, analytical gaps, or areas requiring additional evidence or clarification.
paraphrase: Comprehensive internal feedback will be sought to identify methodological weaknesses, gaps, or areas needing more evidence.

excerpt: We may also use this feedback to improve or refine the report itself.
paraphrase: Feedback may also be used to improve or refine the report.

excerpt: We will usually also seek feedback from trusted external parties with relevant expertise.
paraphrase: Feedback from trusted external experts will usually also be sought.

excerpt: Executive approval: The Risk Report, along with the internal feedback and any available external feedback, will be sent to the CEO and Responsible Scaling Officer (RSO) for final review and approval.
paraphrase: The Risk Report and associated feedback are sent to the CEO and RSO for final review and approval.

excerpt: The CEO and RSO will make the ultimate determination regarding the adequacy of the risk assessment and any downstream deployment or development plans.
paraphrase: The CEO and RSO make the final determination on the adequacy of the risk assessment and related deployment or development plans.

excerpt: Governance notification: Following approval of a Risk Report, the CEO and RSO will promptly share their decision(s), the underlying Risk Report, and internal feedback with both the Board and the LTBT.
paraphrase: After approval, the CEO and RSO promptly share the decision, Risk Report, and internal feedback with the Board and the LTBT.

excerpt: Modified process when marginal risk analysis is important to our case. In the event that marginal risk analysis (see previous section) plays a major role in a decision to move forward, explicit approval of the Risk Report by the Board and LTBT (rather than just the CEO and RSO) will be required.
paraphrase: If marginal risk analysis plays a major role in a decision to proceed, explicit Board and LTBT approval is required instead of just CEO and RSO approval.

excerpt: By "marginal risk analysis," we mean arguing that the risks imposed by our systems in particular are relatively lower when keeping in mind the risks unavoidably posed by other AI systems.
paraphrase: Footnote defines marginal risk analysis as an argument that a system's risks are relatively lower given unavoidable risks from other AI systems.

excerpt: We will publish a public version of our Risk Report.
paraphrase: A public version of the Risk Report will be published.

excerpt: We will aim to minimize redactions to the public version of the report.
paraphrase: The aim is to minimize redactions in the public version of the report.

excerpt: Reasons we may redact material include but are not limited to:
paraphrase: A non-exhaustive list of reasons for redaction follows.

context_stem: Reasons we may redact material include but are not limited to:
excerpt: Legal compliance: To comply with legal obligations on disclosing information, such as export control regulations, national security restrictions, or contractual obligations with third parties.
paraphrase: Redaction may occur to comply with legal disclosure obligations such as export controls, national security, or contractual duties.

context_stem: Reasons we may redact material include but are not limited to:
excerpt: Intellectual property protection: To protect proprietary information, including technical details of our models and training methodologies, trade secrets, or other confidential business information.
paraphrase: Redaction may protect proprietary information such as technical model details, training methods, or trade secrets.

context_stem: Reasons we may redact material include but are not limited to:
excerpt: Public safety considerations: To protect public safety by not disclosing information that could be exploited to cause harm.
paraphrase: Redaction may protect public safety by withholding information that could enable harm.

context_stem: Reasons we may redact material include but are not limited to:
excerpt: Privacy: To protect the personal privacy of individuals.
paraphrase: Redaction may protect individuals' personal privacy.

excerpt: We will work toward a practice of seeking comprehensive, public external review on our Risk Reports.
paraphrase: Anthropic will work toward comprehensive, public external review of its Risk Reports.

excerpt: This means working with one or more third-party organizations that will receive private versions of our Risk Reports (unredacted or with minimal redactions, as discussed below) and publish comprehensive commentary on them.
paraphrase: Third-party organizations will receive private, largely unredacted versions of Risk Reports and publish comprehensive commentary.

excerpt: Commentary will address topics including the quality of our reasoning, the validity of our risk assessments, the overall level of risk, and whether the redactions we've made for the public version are reasonable and appropriate.
paraphrase: External commentary will cover reasoning quality, risk assessment validity, overall risk level, and reasonableness of redactions.

excerpt: Our intent is for external reviewers' judgments to carry significant weight in the eyes of the public as well as our employees.
paraphrase: External reviewer judgments are intended to carry significant weight with both the public and employees.

excerpt: But there are no well-established organizations or procedures for this sort of practice, and we are approaching it as an experiment.
paraphrase: Because no well-established organizations or procedures exist for this practice, it is being approached experimentally.

excerpt: At a minimum, we will complete a full external review process (described below) with at least one external reviewer anytime a Risk Report covers highly capable models and is significantly redacted, defined as follows:
paraphrase: A full external review process with at least one reviewer will be completed whenever a Risk Report covers highly capable models and is significantly redacted, as defined below.

excerpt: A model is "highly capable" if we conclude that it crosses the threshold for automated AI R&D described in Section 1.
paraphrase: A model is deemed highly capable if it crosses the automated AI R&D threshold described in Section 1.

excerpt: "Significantly redacted" means that the redactions omit information a reasonable external safety researcher would consider important in evaluating the overall level of risk, such that a reader of only the public version could not meaningfully assess whether they agree with our conclusions.
paraphrase: Significantly redacted means redactions omit information important to evaluating risk, such that a public-only reader could not meaningfully assess agreement with conclusions.

excerpt: A report shall be deemed significantly redacted if, in the judgment of the RSO, CEO, Board, or LTBT, it meets this description.
paraphrase: A report is deemed significantly redacted if the RSO, CEO, Board, or LTBT judge it meets that description.

excerpt: Note that unredacted reports will be shared with a large number of employees, who will be in a position to raise concerns if they believe the public version meets this description.
paraphrase: Unredacted reports will be shared with many employees, who can raise concerns if they believe the public version is significantly redacted.

excerpt: In addition, upon the LTBT's request, we will conduct a public or private external review of our Risk Report or sections thereof, subject to the procedures outlined below.
paraphrase: At the LTBT's request, a public or private external review of the Risk Report or parts of it will be conducted per the outlined procedures.

excerpt: We will select external reviewers that:
paraphrase: The following criteria guide the selection of external reviewers.

context_stem: We will select external reviewers that:
excerpt: Have significant experience and expertise regarding evaluations for dangerous AI capabilities and propensities.
paraphrase: Reviewers must have significant experience and expertise in evaluating dangerous AI capabilities and propensities.

excerpt: It's particularly important that they be knowledgeable about potential ways such evaluations might be misleading (for example, alignment faking).
paraphrase: Reviewers should particularly understand ways such evaluations could be misleading, such as alignment faking.

context_stem: We will select external reviewers that:
excerpt: Have reputational and other incentives making them likely to be candid about their assessment of risks, rather than focused on writing comments that Anthropic will approve of.
paraphrase: Reviewers should have incentives to be candid about risk assessments rather than to please Anthropic.

excerpt: For example, external review parties should not be teams whose revenue, reputation and success depend entirely on Anthropic and similar companies continuing to work with them.
paraphrase: External reviewers should not be entirely dependent on Anthropic and similar companies for revenue, reputation, or success.

context_stem: We will select external reviewers that:
excerpt: Do not have conflicts of interest with respect to Anthropic.
paraphrase: Reviewers must not have conflicts of interest regarding Anthropic.

context_stem: Do not have conflicts of interest with respect to Anthropic.
excerpt: At a minimum, a reviewing organization itself may not have a financial interest in Anthropic; and the individuals involved in conducting the review, as well as anyone above them in the reporting chain within their organization, may not have a financial interest in Anthropic or close personal relationships with anyone at Anthropic (i.e., family relationships, romantic relationships, or shared living arrangements).
paraphrase: Neither the reviewing organization nor individuals conducting or overseeing the review may hold financial interests in Anthropic or close personal relationships with Anthropic staff.

excerpt: In selecting external reviewers, we will consult with the Board and obtain the approval of the LTBT.
paraphrase: The Board will be consulted and LTBT approval obtained in selecting external reviewers.

excerpt: The external review process will involve sharing the Risk Report with one or more external reviewers within one week of submitting the same report to our Board and LTBT.
paraphrase: External reviewers receive the Risk Report within one week of its submission to the Board and LTBT.

excerpt: We will ask the external reviewers to provide public commentary on our report within 30 days of receipt.
paraphrase: External reviewers are asked to provide public commentary within 30 days of receiving the report.

excerpt: We will try to work toward a process that involves the full external review being completed prior to Board/LTBT review (and may require this later).
paraphrase: Efforts will be made toward completing full external review before Board/LTBT review, potentially becoming a requirement later.

excerpt: For purposes of external review, the only redactions to the Risk Report will be those necessary to comply with legal prohibitions or to maintain our legal rights.7
paraphrase: For external review purposes, redactions are limited to those legally necessary or needed to preserve legal rights.

excerpt: We expect that we will also invest some time in answering follow-up questions from parties doing external review.

excerpt: We also introduced the new concepts of Capability Thresholds and Required Safeguards. This change allows for more targeted application of safeguards based on specific capabilities, rather than broad model categories.
paraphrase: New concepts of Capability Thresholds and Required Safeguards were introduced, enabling more targeted safeguard application.

paraphrase: The prior ARA threshold was replaced with a checkpoint concept for autonomous AI capabilities.

paraphrase: A new threshold was added for AI systems capable of significantly advancing AI development.

locator: Changelog / v2.0 / AI R&D threshold added

paraphrase: Instead of prespecified evaluations, an affirmative case is now required showing models are sufficiently distant from Capability Thresholds.

locator: Changelog / v2.0 / Testing for Capability Thresholds

paraphrase: Because accurate tests change often, the new approach is more practical than requiring Board pre-approval of evaluations.

paraphrase: The comprehensive assessment cadence changed to 4x Effective Compute or six months of post-training enhancements, up from three months.

paraphrase: The prior three-month cadence pushed teams toward frequent evaluation at the expense of comprehensive testing and methodology improvement.

paraphrase: Specific prior methodology details (like 1% compute for elicitation or a 6x buffer) were replaced with general requirements to match adversary effort and estimate scaling impacts.

locator: Changelog / v2.0 / Less prescriptive evaluation methodology
excerpt: We have found that specific methodologies may become outdated when new research developments are introduced.
paraphrase: Specific methodologies risk becoming outdated as new research emerges.
